settings.title: Check-ups and dental cleans
settings.lead: Prevention is far better than cure. Regular check-ups let us spot small problems early, before they become bigger, costlier ones.
settings.alt: A dentist in blue gloves examining a smiling patient’s teeth

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
At Redlynch Dental, we welcome all new patients of all ages. If you are visiting us for the first time, we recommend starting with a thorough consultation and dental clean.

By attending regularly for check-ups and cleans, we can recognise and treat the early signs of potential problems so they don’t progress. This saves you time and money, and helps you keep your own natural teeth looking great and functioning comfortably for years to come.

settings.title: What we do at your visit

settings.editor: We take the time to look at the whole picture, not just one tooth. At a comprehensive check-up and clean we:

items.title: Examine your teeth and gums
items.text: A careful check of every tooth, your gums and the soft tissues of your mouth.

items.title: Assess your jaw joints
items.text: We check how your jaw moves and how your teeth meet when you bite.

items.title: Take the X-rays you need
items.text: Both close-up and full-face X-rays where necessary, so we can see what isn’t visible to the eye.

items.title: Show you what we see
items.text: We take photos of any potential problems so you can see them for yourself.

items.title: Scale, clean and polish
items.text: Removing plaque and hardened tartar from your teeth and along the gum line, followed by a topical fluoride treatment.

items.title: Give you a printed treatment plan
items.text: The most accurate estimate we can give of the time and cost involved in restoring your mouth to full health, function and appearance.

settings.editor: Tooth decay and gum disease are among the most common health problems in Australia, and both can progress without obvious pain in the early stages. A regular examination and clean helps find problems while they are small and simpler to treat. Your dentist will recommend how often you should come in, based on your own oral health.

settings.content: Between visits: brush twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth, limit sugary food and drinks, and drink tap water. These everyday habits make the biggest difference to your teeth.

settings.editor: Bleeding gums when you brush or floss can be an early sign of gum inflammation (gingivitis). Left untreated, gum disease can progress and affect the bone that supports your teeth. A professional clean, combined with good daily care, is the starting point for healthier gums.

items.question: How often should I have a check-up and clean?
items.answer: It depends on your oral health, so your dentist will recommend an interval that suits you. Many people come in every six to twelve months, but some people benefit from more frequent visits.

items.question: Do I need X-rays every time?
items.answer: Not always. X-rays are taken when they are needed to check areas that can’t be seen with the eye, such as between teeth, under existing fillings or below the gum line. Your dentist will explain why any X-ray is recommended.

settings.title: Children’s dentistry
settings.lead: Your child’s early experiences at the dentist shape how they feel about dental care for life. We keep visits calm, positive and fun.
settings.alt: A smiling young girl sitting in a dental chair

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
Your child’s early experiences at the dentist are so important in shaping their future attitude towards their dental health. Fun, positive early experiences are the best way to make sure your child doesn’t develop unnecessary long-term dental fears.

Early diagnosis and treatment of any problems with your child’s teeth can help reduce the time and money needed to fix them, and prevent unnecessary discomfort.

Bulk billing for eligible children. Redlynch Dental bulk bills eligible children under the Child Dental Benefits Schedule (CDBS). Not every child is eligible, so please ask our team about your child’s situation when you book. See payments and fees.

items.title: Start early
items.text: Bringing children in early, before there is a problem, means their first experiences of the dental chair are relaxed and positive.

items.title: Gentle, patient care
items.text: We take things slowly and explain each step in child-friendly language, so children feel at ease.

items.title: Distraction helps

items.title: Parents are part of it

settings.title: Looking after little teeth at home

settings.editor:
A few simple habits make a big difference:

  • Clean your baby’s teeth as soon as they appear, using a soft toothbrush. Under 18 months, only use toothpaste if your child’s dentist recommends it.
  • From 18 months to 5 years, brush twice a day with a soft toothbrush and a small pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste. Your dentist may recommend a different toothpaste if your child is at high risk of decay.
  • Children should spit out toothpaste after brushing, rather than swallowing it or rinsing.
  • Help with brushing until your child can do it well on their own. By about 9 years of age, most children can brush and floss their own teeth.
  • Offer water between meals, limit sweet snacks and drinks, and avoid putting a baby to bed with a bottle of milk or juice.

Baby teeth matter. They help children chew, speak and smile with confidence, and they hold space for the adult teeth that follow.

settings.title: Cosmetic veneers
settings.lead: Thin shells of porcelain, made for your smile and bonded to the front of your teeth. Veneers can address gaps, chips, staining and worn or uneven teeth.
settings.alt: A row of thin, translucent porcelain veneers on a dark background

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
In a similar way to false fingernails, veneers are thin shells of porcelain that are bonded to your teeth to give the appearance of a beautiful smile. Veneers can correct gappy teeth, crooked teeth, discoloured or stained teeth, and short and worn teeth.

Veneers have the potential to last many years when done correctly.

settings.title: Is a veneer right for you?

settings.editor: Veneers are often considered for:

items.title: Gaps and uneven teeth
items.text: Closing small gaps or improving the look of slightly crooked or irregular teeth.

items.title: Discolouration
items.text: Teeth that are stained or discoloured and don’t respond well to whitening.

items.title: Chips and wear
items.text: Front teeth that are chipped, short or worn down over time.

items.title: Shape and proportion
items.text: Teeth that are small, oddly shaped or out of proportion with the rest of your smile.

settings.editor: Veneers aren’t the right answer for everyone. Teeth need to be healthy, and active decay or gum disease must be treated first. Your dentist may also suggest alternatives such as whitening, tooth-coloured bonding, clear aligners or crowns, depending on your goals.

settings.content:
Not sure veneers are the right option?

Compare whitening, composite bonding, porcelain veneers, clear aligners and crowns, with what each involves and costs, and book a cosmetic consultation.

settings.editor: Treatment usually takes two appointments.

items.title: First appointment
items.text: Your teeth are prepared and impressions are taken so your veneers are made to fit your teeth and suit your smile. Preparation may involve removing a small amount of enamel so the final veneers aren’t bulky. Using high-precision magnification and high-quality porcelain helps keep enamel removal to a minimum, and sometimes none is needed. Temporary veneers are fitted while your custom veneers are made in the laboratory.

items.title: Final appointment
items.text: Your temporary veneers are gently removed and your permanent veneers are bonded to your teeth. Any adjustments are made then and there, and we run through how to care for your new smile.

settings.editor:
• Where enamel is removed, the change can’t be reversed, and the tooth will need a veneer or other restoration from then on.
  • Porcelain veneers can chip or crack, and may eventually need replacing.
  • Habits such as grinding your teeth, biting nails or opening packets with your teeth increase the risk of damage. A night guard may be recommended.
  • Veneers don’t change colour with whitening, so any whitening is usually done first.

Any surgical or invasive procedure carries risks. Before proceeding, you should seek a second opinion from an appropriately qualified health practitioner.

items.question: How long do veneers last?
items.answer: Veneers can last many years with good care, but they are not permanent. How long they last depends on the material, your bite, your habits and how well you look after them. Your dentist can talk through what to expect for your situation.

items.question: Will my teeth need to be shaved down?
items.answer: Often a small amount of enamel is removed so the veneers sit naturally. Using magnification and high-quality porcelain helps keep this to a minimum, and in some cases none is needed. Your dentist will explain what is planned for your teeth before you begin.

items.question: Do veneers look natural?
items.answer: Veneers are custom-made for your smile, with the shade and shape planned with you, so they can look very natural.

settings.title: Crowns and bridges
settings.lead: A crown reinforces a weakened tooth so you can keep it. A bridge fills the gap left by a missing tooth with a fixed, natural-looking replacement.
settings.alt: Illustration of a porcelain crown being placed over a prepared tooth

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
If your tooth is broken, decayed or has a large filling, it might need a crown. A crown is a cap that is custom made to fit over your existing tooth, reinforcing it and helping to prevent further breakdown. If your tooth needs a crown, the sooner it is done, the better: it can save you money in the medium to long term and help you keep your own natural teeth.

If you have a missing tooth, a bridge may be the best solution. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth by joining an artificial tooth to the neighbouring natural teeth. Bridges are fixed in place and look, feel and function like natural teeth.

People who have lost teeth may feel self-conscious about smiling or talking. Chewing difficulties caused by tooth loss can also affect eating habits, which can lead to other health problems.

Dental implants offer a well-established way to replace missing teeth. The resulting tooth or teeth are fixed in place and non-removable.

settings.editor: A dental implant is a small titanium post placed in the jawbone, where it acts like a tooth root. Once it has healed and bonded with the bone, it supports a crown, a bridge or a denture. Unlike a bridge, a single implant doesn’t rely on the neighbouring teeth for support.

items.title: Protects neighbouring teeth

settings.editor: What counts as a dental emergency

settings.title: If it hurts, it’s broken or it’s swollen, call us.

settings.editor: Dental emergencies are often serious, and if left untreated they can get worse quickly. A dental emergency may include:

items.title: Painful tooth or gums
items.text: Throbbing, constant or night-time pain, or pain when biting, can be a sign of infection or deep decay.
items.extra: Take pain relief as directed and avoid very hot, cold or sweet foods. Call us.

items.title: Broken teeth and fillings
items.text: Even without pain, a broken tooth or lost filling can crack further, trap food or expose the nerve.
items.extra: Keep any broken pieces, rinse gently, and avoid chewing on that side.

items.title: Facial swelling
items.text: Swelling of the face, jaw or gums can mean an infection that needs prompt attention.
items.extra: Call us straight away. If swelling affects breathing, swallowing or your eye, call 000.

items.title: Trauma to the face, teeth or gums
items.text: A knock or fall that chips, loosens, moves or knocks out a tooth, or injures the gums or lips.
items.extra: Knocked-out tooth? Hold it by the crown, keep it moist in milk, and call immediately.

items.title: Broken or lost denture
items.text: A cracked, broken or lost denture can make eating and speaking difficult.
items.extra: Keep all the pieces and don’t try to glue it yourself. Call us.

settings.title: Fillings
settings.lead: Treating tooth decay early saves time, effort and money, and helps you keep your natural tooth. We repair decayed teeth with white, tooth-coloured filling material.
settings.alt: A smiling young boy sitting in a dental chair

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
Dental decay is one of the most common health issues we face as a population. If left untreated, decay progresses through the tooth until the nerve dies and an infection develops. At that point, the only treatment options are root canal therapy or extraction.

By treating decay early, we save a lot of time, effort and money. To treat early tooth decay, we remove all of the decayed part of the tooth and replace it with a white filling material.

items.title: Enamel
items.text: Early decay starts in the hard outer layer of the tooth. It often causes no symptoms, which is why regular check-ups matter.

items.title: Dentine
items.text: Once decay reaches the softer layer underneath, it can spread more quickly and the tooth may become sensitive to sweet, hot or cold.

items.title: Nerve (pulp)
items.text: If decay reaches the nerve, it can cause pain and infection. Treatment then usually means root canal therapy or extraction.

items.title: Numbing
items.text: Local anaesthetic is used where needed so you are comfortable.

items.title: Removing decay
items.text: All of the decayed part of the tooth is carefully removed and the tooth is cleaned.

items.title: Restoring
items.text: Tooth-coloured filling material is placed in layers, shaped and polished to fit your bite.

settings.editor: A filling repairs the tooth, but it doesn’t stop new decay from forming around it. Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, cleaning between your teeth and keeping sugary foods and drinks to a minimum all help your fillings, and your teeth, last longer.

items.question: Do white fillings last as long as silver ones?
items.answer: Modern tooth-coloured materials are durable for most situations. How long any filling lasts depends on its size, where it is, your bite and your oral hygiene. Large fillings in back teeth may eventually need a crown.

items.question: How do I know if I need a filling?
items.answer: Early decay often has no symptoms. It is usually found at a check-up, on X-rays or during an examination. Sensitivity to sweet or cold, a rough edge or a visible hole are also reasons to book in.

items.question: Can I eat after a filling?
items.answer: Tooth-coloured fillings are set during the appointment. If you have had local anaesthetic, wait until the numbness wears off before eating so you don’t bite your cheek or tongue.

settings.title: Root canal therapy
settings.lead: When the nerve inside a tooth is inflamed beyond repair or has died, root canal therapy can save the tooth and avoid the need to remove it.
settings.alt: Diagram showing the stages of root canal treatment, from an infected tooth to a crowned, root-filled tooth

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
Root canal therapy is needed when the nerve in your tooth is inflamed beyond repair or has died. This can happen because of deep decay or an injury or knock to the tooth. During treatment, the nerve is removed from the tooth and replaced with a filling material.

Despite what you may have heard, the majority of root canal treatments are completed comfortably under local anaesthetic. Root canal treatment can be a safe and long-lasting option for patients who want to save their natural teeth and avoid having them removed.

settings.title: Signs you may need a root canal

settings.editor:
• Lingering pain, especially when biting or chewing
  • Sensitivity to heat or cold that lasts after the trigger is gone
  • Swelling or tenderness in the gum near a tooth, or a pimple on the gum
  • A tooth that has darkened after a knock

Sometimes there are no symptoms at all, and the problem is found on an X-ray.

items.title: Access
items.text: The tooth is numbed and a small opening is made to reach the canals inside the root.

items.title: Cleaning
items.text: The inflamed or infected nerve tissue is removed, and the canals are cleaned and shaped.

items.title: Sealing
items.text: The canals are filled and sealed, and the tooth is closed with a filling.

items.title: Protecting
items.text: A crown is often recommended afterwards, especially for back teeth, to protect the tooth from breaking.

settings.editor: Treatment often takes more than one appointment. Your dentist will explain the plan for your tooth.

settings.content: Swelling or severe pain? A tooth infection can spread. Call us promptly, and see emergency dental care. If swelling affects your breathing or swallowing, call 000.

items.answer: Most root canal treatment is carried out comfortably under local anaesthetic. The tooth may feel tender for a few days afterwards, and we will advise you on pain relief.

items.question: Why not just take the tooth out?
items.answer: Keeping your natural tooth helps you chew properly and stops neighbouring teeth from drifting. A missing tooth may also need replacing later with an implant, bridge or denture. Your dentist will explain the pros and cons of each option.

items.question: Will I need a crown afterwards?
items.answer: Often, particularly for back teeth, because root-filled teeth can become more brittle. See crowns and bridges.

settings.title: Teeth whitening
settings.lead: Professional whitening is a safe and effective way to brighten your smile. A whitening gel is applied to your teeth to lift discolouration that has built up over time.
settings.meta:
Philips Zoom whitening system
Supervised by your dentist
settings.alt: A smiling mother and young daughter hugging

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
Professional teeth whitening is a safe and effective way to brighten your smile. A specially designed bleach is applied to your teeth, absorbing into your enamel and removing discolouration that has built up over time. The procedure is straightforward and takes very little of your time.

We exclusively use the Philips Zoom whitening system, which we believe is the best on the market.

settings.editor:
Many people are good candidates for whitening. The main exception is fillings, crowns or caps on your front teeth. These won’t whiten like your natural teeth, and can leave your smile looking patchy. If that is the case, the answer may be as simple as replacing old fillings with lighter ones to match, or veneers may be a better, longer-lasting option.

Whitening isn’t suitable for everyone. Decay, gum problems and some types of sensitivity or staining need to be checked and managed first, so a check-up is the best place to start.

items.title: Safety
items.text: When a whitening product is recommended and supervised by your dental professional, the procedure has proven to be very safe and does not cause permanent damage to your teeth.

items.title: Avoid risky products
items.text: Some whitening systems sold online contain very high concentrations of bleaching agent that can damage your teeth. Your dentist will never recommend these.

settings.editor: Some patients notice mild sensitivity during whitening. This is temporary, and returns to normal once you stop. If bleach trays are overfilled, you may notice a slight burning sensation and whitening of the gums. Again, this is temporary and settles fairly quickly once the gel is rinsed away.

How long whitening lasts varies from person to person and depends a lot on diet and lifestyle. Tea, coffee, red wine and smoking stain teeth more quickly. On average, whitening may need to be repeated around every six months.

settings.title: Wisdom teeth
settings.lead: Most people get their wisdom teeth from their late teens to early twenties, and for many they cause problems. An assessment and X-ray will show whether yours need attention.
settings.alt: A panoramic dental X-ray with the four wisdom teeth highlighted

settings.label: From the Redlynch Dental team
settings.content:
Wisdom teeth are molars that grow at the very back of your mouth. Unfortunately for most people, they are an inconvenient part of early adulthood.

For some patients, conservative treatment may be all that is needed. For others, removing the problem wisdom tooth is often necessary. As a general rule, if a wisdom tooth does need to be removed, the sooner the better: delaying can increase the difficulty and cost of the procedure.

items.title: Pain and swelling
items.text: Around a partly erupted tooth, often coming and going.

items.title: Infection
items.text: Food and bacteria trapped under the gum can cause infection, bad breath or a bad taste.

items.title: Damage to the next tooth
items.text: Decay and gum disease in the tooth directly in front of the wisdom tooth.

settings.editor: Wisdom teeth can also crowd other teeth. Importantly, many wisdom tooth problems don’t cause pain, which is why an assessment and X-ray are so valuable.

items.title: Consultation
items.text: One of our dentists assesses your wisdom teeth and takes an X-ray, then tells you whether they need to be removed.

items.title: Clear costing
items.text: If removal is recommended, you receive a detailed costing of the procedure, and we find an appointment that suits you.

items.title: Removal
items.text: Most wisdom teeth can be removed in the chair under local anaesthetic while you are awake. Some cases are referred to an oral surgeon for removal under sedation or general anaesthetic.

settings.content: Call us if pain or swelling around a wisdom tooth is getting worse, or you have trouble opening your mouth. If swelling affects your breathing or swallowing, call 000.

items.question: I’m having problems with my wisdom teeth. What should I do?
items.answer: Call us to arrange a consultation with one of our dentists. We will assess your wisdom teeth, take an X-ray and let you know whether they need to be removed. If they do, we will give you a detailed costing and find an appointment that suits you.

items.question: How much does it cost to have a wisdom tooth removed?
items.answer:
The practice’s published guide is $200 to $400 per tooth for removal under local anaesthetic while you are awake in the chair. Some cases need referral to an oral surgeon for removal under sedation or general anaesthetic, and the cost will differ.

Your exact cost depends on the tooth and is confirmed in writing after your assessment.

items.question: I’m anxious about having them removed. What can be done?
items.answer: Our dentists and support team are experienced in managing wisdom teeth. Where appropriate, a sedative can be prescribed for you to take before the appointment to help you relax.

items.question: Do wisdom teeth always need to be removed?
items.answer: No. Some people have enough room for the wisdom tooth to come through normally, and can brush and floss it to keep it clean. However, this is not very common.

items.question: My wisdom teeth aren’t sore. Can they still cause problems?
items.answer: Yes. Many of the problems wisdom teeth cause are painless, so it is important to have them assessed and X-rayed.

items.question: Are you accepting new patients?
items.answer: Yes. Redlynch Dental welcomes new patients of all ages.

items.answer: We recommend starting with a thorough consultation and dental clean. items.question: How often should I have a check-up?
items.answer: Your dentist will recommend an interval based on your oral health. Many people come in every six to twelve months.

items.question: How should I look after my teeth at home?
items.answer: Brush twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth every day, limit sugary foods and drinks, drink tap water, and keep up regular check-ups.

items.question: Why are X-rays needed?
items.answer: X-rays show areas the eye can’t see, such as decay between teeth, under fillings or below the gum line, and the position of wisdom teeth. Your dentist will only recommend X-rays you need.

items.question: My gums bleed when I brush. Should I worry?
items.answer: Bleeding gums can be an early sign of gum inflammation. It is worth booking a check-up and clean. See check-ups and cleans.

items.question: When should my child first see a dentist?
items.answer: Children should see a dentist by the time their first tooth appears, or by their first birthday. Call us to book.

items.question: Do you bulk bill children?
items.answer: Yes, for eligible children. Redlynch Dental bulk bills eligible children under the Child Dental Benefits Schedule (CDBS). Please ask our team about your child’s eligibility when you book.

items.question: What toothpaste should my child use?
items.answer: A small pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste, twice a day, from 18 months to 5 years. Under 18 months, only use toothpaste if your child’s dentist recommends it. Ask us if you’re unsure.

items.question: Does my child need a mouthguard?
items.answer: Children who play contact sport should wear a mouthguard. A mouthguard custom-made by a dentist gives the most protection. See mouthguards.

items.question: What counts as a dental emergency?
items.answer: Painful teeth or gums, broken teeth or fillings, facial swelling, trauma to the face, teeth or gums, and broken or lost dentures. Emergency dental care.

items.question: Can I be seen the same day?
items.answer: Specific appointments are reserved every day for emergencies, and the team will always strive to see you as soon as possible. Call as early as you can.

items.question: When should I call 000 instead?
items.answer: If swelling affects your breathing, swallowing or eye, bleeding won’t stop, you have a serious head or facial injury, or you feel very unwell, call 000 or go to your nearest emergency department.

items.question: Should I choose whitening or veneers?
items.answer: Whitening brightens your natural teeth but won’t change fillings, crowns or the shape of teeth. Veneers change shape and colour but involve more treatment. Your dentist can help you decide. See whitening and veneers.

items.question: Am I suitable for dental implants?
items.answer: It depends on your bone, gum health and general health. The practice offers a complimentary implant consultation, with a 3D X-ray, to assess suitability. Dental implants.

items.question: How long does clear aligner treatment take?
items.answer: It depends on your needs. Some minor cases take as little as seven weeks, but average treatment is around 12 to 18 months. Clear aligners.

items.question: Does root canal treatment hurt?
items.answer: Most root canal treatment is carried out comfortably under local anaesthetic. The tooth may be tender for a few days afterwards. Root canal therapy.

items.question: How much will my treatment cost?
items.answer: It depends on what you need. After a comprehensive check-up you receive a printed treatment plan with the most accurate estimate we can give of the time and cost involved, and we discuss it with you before treatment starts.

items.question: What payment options do you offer?
items.answer: Payment options include Afterpay, Zip, Fund My Dental and Denticare. Eligibility, fees and terms are set by each provider and may vary. Payments and fees.

items.question: Can I use my health fund?
items.answer: What you can claim depends on your fund and level of extras cover. Ask your fund what you are covered for, and ask our team when you book. The new patient offer is gap free for patients with eligible private health insurance and dental cover.

items.question: Is Medicare available for dental care?
items.answer: Medicare does not cover most general dental care for adults. Eligible children may be covered by the Child Dental Benefits Schedule (CDBS), and Redlynch Dental bulk bills eligible children. Other government dental programs exist for eligible people. Check eligibility with Services Australia or Queensland Health, and ask our team whether a particular program can be used at the practice.

items.title: Teeth whitening
items.text: Supervised whitening after a check for decay, cracks and gum disease, with a shade record so you can see the change. Results vary with the cause of the discolouration. Yellow tones respond best, grey and brown tones less. Fillings and crowns don’t whiten.

items.title: Composite bonding
items.text: Tooth-coloured resin shaped onto the tooth to repair a chip, close a small gap, lengthen a worn edge or cover a mark. Usually one visit, little or no drilling, and reversible. Bonding stains and chips more readily than porcelain and is typically replaced or repaired every five to seven years.

items.title: Porcelain veneers
items.text: Thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of teeth to change colour, shape, length and minor alignment. Veneers resist staining and usually last longer than bonding. Preparing a tooth for a veneer usually removes a thin layer of enamel, which is not reversible, so this is a decision to make with full information.

items.title: Clear aligners
items.text: A series of clear, removable aligners that move teeth gradually. Suitability is assessed first with a scan. Treatment times vary with the case. Aligners need to be worn most of the day to work, and retainers are needed afterwards to hold the result.

items.title: Crowns
items.text: For teeth that are heavily filled, cracked or badly worn, a crown covers the whole tooth and restores its shape and strength. More tooth preparation than a veneer.

settings.editor: Step by step

items.title: Consultation
items.text: Tell your dentist what you don’t like. They examine your teeth and gums, take photos and a digital scan, and check that your mouth is healthy enough for cosmetic work. Decay and gum disease are treated first.

items.title: Options and costs
items.text: You go home with a written plan showing the options that suit you, what each involves, how long it lasts, what it costs and what to consider. There is no obligation to proceed.

items.title: Treatment
items.text: Simple options can be done in one or two visits. Veneers, crowns and clear aligners run across several appointments.

items.title: Looking after the result
items.text: Your dentist will explain what each treatment needs to stay looking good, from avoiding staining foods after whitening to wearing retainers after clear aligner treatment.

Before you commit

Cosmetic treatment can change the colour, shape and position of teeth, within limits set by your own teeth, gums and bite.

Your dentist will tell you what is realistic for your case before you commit, and will say so if they think a treatment won’t give you what you’re after. Results differ between patients and no outcome can be guaranteed.

• Veneers and crownsThey involve removing tooth structure and are not reversible. Teeth may be sensitive afterwards, and veneers and crowns can chip or come away and need replacing over time.
  • WhiteningIt can cause temporary sensitivity and does not change the colour of fillings, crowns or veneers.
  • Clear alignersThey require daily commitment. Teeth can move back if retainers aren’t worn.
  • Healthy teeth and gumsAll cosmetic work needs healthy teeth and gums underneath it and the same regular check-ups as natural teeth.

items.question: Which option is right for me?
items.answer: It depends on what you want to change and the condition of your teeth. Bonding and whitening suit small changes and keep your options open. Veneers suit bigger changes in colour and shape. Clear aligners suit position. Your consultation sorts this out.

items.question: Can I have a trial before veneers?
items.answer: Your dentist can show you the planned shape and length using a mock-up on your teeth or on the scan, so you see the direction before anything is prepared.

items.question: How long does whitening last?
items.answer: Typically one to three years depending on diet, smoking and how you look after your teeth. Top-up treatment is available.

items.question: Will veneers look fake?
items.answer: Veneers are made to a colour and shape agreed with you. Most patients ask for a result that looks natural, and the mock-up stage is where that gets decided.

items.question: Do clear aligners work for adults?
items.answer: Yes, provided the teeth and gums are healthy and the case suits aligners. Some cases are better treated with braces, and your dentist will say so.

settings.title: Who asks about full arch implants

items.text: Your full denture slips when you eat or talk, or you use adhesive every day.
You have lost most of the teeth in one jaw, or your remaining teeth are loose, decayed or breaking.
You have been told all your teeth need removing and want a fixed alternative to a conventional denture.
You have an implant-retained denture and want teeth that stay in.

settings.editor: The treatment

A full arch replaces all the teeth in the upper or lower jaw on a single fixed bridge.

The bridge is supported by four to six dental implants, small titanium posts placed in the jawbone. Once the implants have healed and bonded with the bone, the bridge is secured to them.

At Redlynch Dental, full arch implant treatment is provided by Dr Max Ryu and Dr Louis Fernandez. Dr Nadia Mullins places single dental implants.

  • 4 to 6implants support one fixed bridge for the whole upper or lower jaw.
  • Stays inIt doesn’t come out at night and doesn’t need adhesive.
  • Cared forIt is cleaned in the mouth and reviewed by your dentist like natural teeth.
Step by step
Timing differs between patients. Your dentist will give you a plan and a timeframe for your own treatment.

items.title: Consultation and 3D scan
items.text: Your dentist examines your mouth, takes a 3D X-ray (CBCT) and digital impressions, and talks through your health, your goals and your options. You’ll be told at this stage whether full arch implants suit you.

items.title: Planning
items.text: The implant positions and the shape of the new teeth are planned from the scan before any treatment starts. You receive a written treatment plan with the full cost and the sequence of appointments.

items.title: Implant placement
items.text: The implants are placed in the jawbone under local anaesthetic, and oral sedation is available. Any remaining teeth in that arch are removed at the same appointment if they haven’t been already. Your dentist will explain how your appointments are arranged and what to expect while you heal.

items.title: Healing
items.text: The implants bond with the bone over several months. Temporary bridges or dentures may be offered during healing, depending on your treatment plan and clinical suitability.

items.title: Final teeth
items.text: Once healed, the final bridge is made to match your face, bite and preferences, then fitted and adjusted.

items.title: Reviews
items.text: Regular check-ups to check the implants, the gums and the bridge, and to clean areas you can’t reach at home.

Suitability

Not everyone is suitable.

Your dentist will look at the amount and quality of bone in your jaw, the health of your gums, your general health and any medications, and whether you smoke. Some people need extra procedures first, such as bone grafting.

If a full arch isn’t the right option, your dentist will go through the alternatives with you, including what happens if you choose to do nothing for now:

  • An implant-retained dentureA removable denture that clips onto two or more implants.
  • A conventional dentureA removable full or partial denture.
  • Individual implants and bridgesWhere enough natural teeth remain.

• Surgery and healingIt involves surgery and a healing period of months, with some swelling and discomfort in the first days.
  • Several appointmentsTreatment runs across several appointments, usually over three to six months or longer depending on healing.
  • Daily care and maintenanceThe bridge and implants need daily cleaning and regular professional maintenance. Gum disease around implants can lead to implant loss.
  • Possible complicationsAs with any surgery there are possible complications, including infection, nerve disturbance, implants that don’t bond with the bone, and a bridge that needs repair or replacement over time. Your dentist will discuss the risks that apply to you.
  • Health factorsSmoking, uncontrolled diabetes and some medications affect healing and long-term success.

items.question: How long does the whole process take?
items.answer: Usually three to six months from the first consultation to the final bridge, longer if grafting is needed. Your dentist will give you a timeframe for your own case.

items.question: Will I be without teeth?
items.answer: Temporary bridges or dentures may be offered while the implants heal, depending on your treatment plan and clinical suitability. Your dentist will explain what applies to you before treatment starts.

items.question: Is it painful?
items.answer: Implants are placed under local anaesthetic so you are numb during the procedure. Some swelling, bruising and discomfort is normal for a few days afterwards and is managed with the pain relief your dentist recommends.

items.question: Can I be sedated?
items.answer: Local anaesthetic and oral sedation options are available, including prescribed medication such as Valium (diazepam). General anaesthesia and other sedation options are arranged through referral. Your dentist will talk through which options suit you.

items.question: Am I too old for implants?
items.answer: Age on its own isn’t the deciding factor. Bone, gum health and general health are. Your consultation and 3D scan will show whether implants suit you.

items.question: How do I clean a full arch bridge?
items.answer: Brushing, cleaning under the bridge with the tools your dentist shows you, and regular professional cleans. It’s cleaned in the mouth, not taken out.

items.question: Does my health fund cover it?
items.answer: Extras cover may contribute towards some items. What you get back depends on your policy, so check with your fund using the item numbers in your treatment plan.

posts.title: Why choose dental implants?
posts.excerpt: Dental implants are a simple and proven way to replace one or more missing teeth. Here are the main advantages.
posts.content:
Dental implants are a simple and proven way to replace one or more missing teeth. A titanium screw is placed in the jaw, and a tooth is then placed on top.

What are the advantages of dental implants?

  • Fully fixed in place, so they can’t fall out like a denture
  • Look like a natural tooth
  • Function and chew like a natural tooth
  • Help prevent drifting and movement of the natural teeth around the gap
  • Help prevent the jawbone shrinking away where the tooth has been removed

Is an implant right for you?

Not everyone is suitable for implants, and every case is different. If you would like more information about dental implants, call our friendly team on (07) 4039 4720 to book a consultation. Read more about dental implants at Redlynch Dental, including the three stages of treatment.
